title: Is AI Reading Your Chats? What Really Happens and How to Turn It Off
summary: Yes, most AI chatbots train on your conversations by default. Here is what that actually means, and the exact settings to turn it off for ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude.
body:
If you have ever typed something personal into ChatGPT, Gemini, or Claude and then wondered whether that information is being used to train the AI, you are not alone. It is the single most common privacy question people have about these tools. The short answer: yes, on consumer plans, your chats can be used for training unless you turn off a specific setting. The good news is that turning it off takes about a minute per service.

## What "Training on Your Data" Actually Means

When an AI company says it may use your conversations for training, it means your inputs and the AI's outputs can become part of the dataset used to build future versions of the model. This is how these systems improve over time.

<cite index="2-15,2-16">Consumer ChatGPT conversations are used by default to train OpenAI's future models. Anything you type, including details about your health, finances, work plans, or personal life, could be embedded in training data even if it is never shown to another user.</cite>

This does not mean another person will see your exact words in a response. But your phrasing, questions, and the substance of what you discussed become part of what shapes how the model learns.

## The Key Caveat: You Cannot Undo What Is Already Done

<cite index="3-5">Opting out mostly stops future training, but it rarely removes data already used.</cite> This is the uncomfortable truth about AI training: <cite index="3-17,3-18,3-19">You can stop future training and request deletion of stored data under GDPR or CCPA, but removing data already embedded in a trained model ("machine unlearning") is an unsolved technical problem.</cite>

The takeaway: the earlier you opt out, the more of your data stays out. If you have been using these tools for months without changing settings, some of your conversations may already have been included in a training run.

## ChatGPT: How to Turn Off Training

<cite index="2-7">Training is on by default for Free, Plus, and Pro personal accounts.</cite> <cite index="5-16">Enterprise and API users are excluded from training by default.</cite>

**To opt out:**

1. <cite index="2-17,2-18,2-19,2-20,2-21,2-22,2-23,2-24,2-25,2-26,2-27">Go to chat.openai.com or open the ChatGPT app, signed in to your personal account. Click your profile icon in the top-right corner and select Settings. Go to Data Controls. Find the toggle labeled "Improve the model for everyone" and switch it off.</cite>

<cite index="6-17,6-18">Opting out does not delete your past conversations, does not stop OpenAI from retaining your data for safety monitoring, and does not make your inputs private during transmission. Standard 30-day retention for abuse monitoring persists even with opt-out.</cite>

**One important exception:** <cite index="42-1,42-2,42-3,42-4">Rate an answer with thumbs up or thumbs down and you are giving feedback. OpenAI writes that the entire conversation attached to that feedback may be used to train its models. A rating is the one gesture that can push an entire conversation into training despite the opt-out.</cite>

## Gemini: How to Turn Off Training

<cite index="8-12,8-13">By default, your Gemini conversations are saved, and a sample of them is read by human reviewers and used to improve Google's models.</cite>

**To opt out:**

1. <cite index="33-1,33-17">Go to myactivity.google.com/product/gemini and turn off Keep Activity.</cite>

<cite index="8-1,8-2">Toggling this setting off will stop your chats from being visible in your Gemini activity history. They will also no longer be used to train AI models, with the exception of sending feedback.</cite>

<cite index="14-9">Whether or not you opt out of having your data be used to train Gemini, Google saves your account's chats for up to 72 hours.</cite> <cite index="10-17">Google does not train on Gemini API inputs or outputs by default.</cite>

## Claude: How to Turn Off Training

Claude's story is a bit different. <cite index="33-13,33-14,33-15">Until late 2025, Anthropic did not train on consumer conversations at all, and said so as a selling point. Since 28 August 2025 it does, if you allow it, and allowed chats can be kept for up to five years.</cite>

**To opt out:**

1. <cite index="30-1,30-2">Select your name from the settings menu, then Settings, then Privacy. Under "Help Improve our AI models," click the button to toggle it off.</cite>

<cite index="29-1,29-2,29-3,29-4,29-5,29-6">When you opt out, new chats and coding sessions are not used for model training, and previously stored sessions stop being used in future training runs. It is not retroactive, so data already included in training runs in progress, or in models already trained, is not pulled back out. Retention drops from 5 years to 30 days.</cite>

<cite index="25-7,25-8">There is one caveat when you opt out of Claude's model training. If your conversation is flagged by Anthropic's trust and safety classifiers as potentially violating the Usage Policy, it may still be reviewed and used to improve safety systems.</cite>

<cite index="20-8">The training policy does not apply in the same way to commercial services such as Claude for Work, the Anthropic API, Amazon Bedrock, or Claude through Google Cloud Vertex AI.</cite>

## What Opting Out Does and Does Not Do

**It does:**
- Prevent your future conversations from being used to train new models
- Often reduce how long your data is retained
- Apply immediately to new chats

**It does not:**
- Delete conversations you have already had
- Remove data that was already used in a completed training run
- Stop the provider from temporarily retaining data for safety monitoring
- Prevent your data from being used if you click feedback buttons (ChatGPT and Gemini)

## The Bottom Line

<cite index="3-6">Companies typically opt you in by default; you must opt out manually.</cite> <cite index="3-9">Each takes a minute; settings change often, so re-check periodically.</cite> The toggles move around as these products evolve, so it is worth revisiting your settings every few months.

If you use these tools for anything sensitive, consider using features like Temporary Chat in ChatGPT or Incognito mode in Claude, which are excluded from training regardless of your main settings. And if you want the strongest protections, API and enterprise tiers at all three providers exclude your data from training by default, no toggles required.
